The '''father''' of [[Fir Megsan]] was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] who served the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during<ref name="Lord Praven" /> the [[Great Galactic War]]<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> with the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]].<ref name="Lord Praven" /> In [[3653 BBY]],<ref name="Date" /> the man was present on<ref name="Lord Praven" /> the Republic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] when the Empire [[Sacking of Coruscant|attacked]] the planet. During the fighting, Megsan's [[Parent/Legends|father]] was [[Death/Legends|killed]] by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Praven]], causing the young Megsan to set a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith Pureblood]] in an attempt to gain revenge.<ref name="Lord Praven" />

==Behind the scenes==
Fir Megsan's father was mentioned in the [[2011]] [[BioWare]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]], ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', in a message to players of the [[Hero of Tython|Jedi Knight]] character who have chosen at least one [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] option after their [[Duel on the Esus Mesa|confrontation]] with Lord Praven on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]<ref name="Desert Duel">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Desert Duel|Tatooine}}</ref> in [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="Act I">{{TOR dates|1}}</ref> instead of convincing him to become a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] for [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] points.<ref name="Desert Duel" /> In the message, Megsan thanks the player for avenging their father, explaining that he had died during the Sacking of Coruscant and that everyone who pursued the bounty that was placed on Lord Praven "caught a serious case of corpse."<ref name="Lord Praven" /> However, this article assumes the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] to be a light side character, and so Megsan's bounty is assumed to never have been fulfilled.
